results.summary_before: This design outputs ASCII-encoded text sequences character by character, selecting between two texts using a 2-bit input. One text is the beginning of a traditional Guatemalan song, and the other lists the project participants' names. An internal counter increments each clock cycle until a limit is reached, then resets to repeat the sequence. Testing requires an external microcontroller to read the 8 output pins synchronously and forward the characters over UART to a computer terminal; the author tested it with a TIVA C and an FPGA.

results.summary_before: This design accepts an 8-bit event signal with x, y, p, and t parameters and outputs the signal only when the p bit is high, filtering it to reduce noise. It also includes a clock divider and binary-to-decimal logic driving a 7-segment display, with the lower counter bits exposed on the bidirectional pins. The input pins program a 24-bit compare value that sets the counting rate. The documentation describes the counter behavior in detail but gives only a brief description of the denoising function.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-channel PWM controller for LED brightness, using an exponential (X^3) duty cycle curve to provide linear perceived brightness with 8-bit input. It can be controlled either by the ui inputs or via I2C, with the first I2C write switching to I2C mode. Testing can be done by adjusting DIP switches to see different brightness levels on a 7-segment LED display. External hardware includes LEDs and optionally an I2C master.

results.summary_before: This analog project implements a Gilbert cell mixer for up and down conversion of signals, with both internal and external local oscillator options. The digital control part can generate internal LO signals at different frequencies or pass an external LO to the analog mixer. Testing requires biasing the input ports with 900-950 mV and applying a differential signal of about 20 mV peak-to-peak, typically using a custom interface PCB. Silicon tests confirm successful downconversion from 32 MHz RF and 30 MHz LO to a 2 MHz IF, and the author notes it works well with both internal and external LO sources.

results.summary_before: This design is an 8-bit digital-to-analog converter that uses successive approximation to convert a digital input into an analog output. It requires an external analog comparator and a resistor array to function, as indicated by the pin names and description. The conversion process uses nonlinear sampling, and the design can be tested by providing comparator values and checking the digital outputs. The documentation is brief and does not provide detailed schematics or test results.
